newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARLINS SIGN SHEFFIELD TO $60 MILLION EXTENSION.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARLINS SIGN SHEFFIELD TO $60 MILLION EXTENSION.

text.p: The free-spending Florida Marlins, who spared no expense hiring talent this off-season, took care of star outfielder Gary Sheffield on Wednesday with a contract extension believed to exceed $60 million.

The Marlins doled out $89 million in the free agent market in adding such stars as ace hurler Alex Fernandez and sluggers Bobby Bonilla and Moises Alou, and spent another $7 million to sign manager Jim Leyland.
The package deal with Sheffield, 28, covers six years with a one-year club option and is among the richest ever awarded.

"I'm in orbit somewhere right now," said Sheffield, who was born in Tampa. "I'm just spaced out and happy, because you never thought that you can actually get a deal like this and be at home doing it, and it's just great to be here."

San Francisco Giants outfielder Barry Bonds, who signed a two-year, $23 million extension in the off-season, is the highest-paid player in baseball at $11.5 million annually. Albert Belle signed a five-year, $55 million free agent deal with the Chicago White Sox.

The Marlins apparently waited to announce the signing for luxury tax purposes. Any extension signed after the start of the 1997 season does not count against baseball's new luxury tax, which assesses a tariff of 35 percent above a certain threshold.
"After they signed all the players, especially the manager in Jim Leyland, I knew that I wanted to be a Florida Marlin," said Sheffield.

Sheffield has played the last three and a half seasons with the Marlins and set career-highs with 42 homers and 120 RBI last season. He led the National League with an on-base percentage of .465 and batted .314 with 142 walks in 1996.
Sheffield, a three-time All-Star, was acquired by Florida from the San Diego Padres in exchange for three players in June 1993.
Sheffield contended for the Triple Crown in 1992 for the Padres when he won the batting title with a .330 average and had 33 homers and 100 RBI.
